senses.definition: to leave hurriedly and secretly, typically to avoid arrest or to escape with stolen money
senses.example: The treasurer absconded with the club's funds.

senses.definition: clever or skillful in using the hands or mind
senses.example: The adroit negotiator found a deal that suited both sides.

senses.definition: without a clearly defined shape or form
senses.example: The plan was still an amorphous set of ideas.

senses.definition: approval or praise
senses.example: The proposal met with the approbation of the whole committee.

senses.definition: (of an appearance) to fail to give a true impression of something
senses.example: His cheerful smile belied his nervousness.

senses.definition: to show something to be false
senses.example: The strong sales figures belie claims that the brand is dying.

senses.definition: showing a casual and cheerful indifference considered to be callous or improper
senses.example: He showed a blithe disregard for the rules.

senses.definition: happy or carefree
senses.example: The children ran down the beach in blithe high spirits.

senses.definition: bold and without shame
senses.example: It was a brazen lie, told to their faces.

senses.definition: to polish something, especially metal, by rubbing
senses.example: The craftsman burnished the brass handles until they shone.

senses.definition: to enhance or improve a reputation or image
senses.example: The charity work helped burnish the company's image.

senses.definition: to admit that something is true or valid after first denying or resisting it
senses.example: She conceded that her plan had flaws.

senses.definition: to surrender or yield something that one possesses
senses.example: The champion conceded the game after only twenty moves.

senses.definition: to yearn to possess or have something, especially something belonging to another
senses.example: He coveted his neighbor's sports car.

senses.definition: neatly skillful and quick in one's movements
senses.example: With a few deft strokes, the artist sketched a face.

senses.definition: to publicly declare to be wrong or evil
senses.example: The government denounced the attack.

senses.definition: having had all moisture removed; dried out
senses.example: Desiccated leaves crunched underfoot.

senses.definition: lacking interest, passion or energy
senses.example: The book is a desiccated account of what was a thrilling war.

senses.definition: not candid or sincere, typically by pretending that one knows less about something than one really does
senses.example: It was disingenuous of him to claim he'd never seen the email.

senses.definition: to conceal one's true motives, feelings or beliefs
senses.example: He dissembled, pretending to be pleased with the gift.

senses.definition: a person who opposes official policy, especially that of an authoritarian state
senses.example: The dissident spent years in prison for his writing.

senses.definition: to involve someone deeply in an argument, conflict or difficult situation
senses.example: The company became embroiled in a long legal battle.

senses.definition: a person or thing that is a perfect example of a particular quality or type
senses.example: The hotel is the epitome of luxury.

senses.definition: to cause someone to be no longer close or affectionate to someone; to alienate
senses.example: Their quarrel estranged the two brothers for years.

senses.definition: to hold someone or something in very high regard; to think or speak very highly of
senses.example: Poets have exalted the beauty of the region for centuries.

senses.definition: to raise to a higher rank or a position of greater power
senses.example: The general was exalted to the rank of marshal.

senses.definition: still in existence; surviving
senses.example: Only two copies of the manuscript are extant.

senses.definition: spoken or done without preparation
senses.example: She gave an extemporaneous speech when the guest of honor was delayed.

senses.definition: to openly disregard a rule, law or convention
senses.example: The company flouted safety regulations for years.

words.note: Flout means to openly disregard a rule; flaunt means to show off.

senses.definition: to instigate or stir up an undesirable or violent sentiment or course of action
senses.example: Agents were accused of fomenting unrest in the region.

senses.definition: patient self-control; restraint and tolerance
senses.example: The teacher showed great forbearance with the unruly class.

senses.definition: friendly and cheerful
senses.example: Our genial host showed us around the farm.

senses.definition: a person or thing that announces or signals the approach of another
senses.example: The first crocuses are harbingers of spring.

senses.definition: unchanging over time or unable to be changed
senses.example: Some believe human nature is immutable.

senses.definition: (of a person or their tendencies) not able to be corrected, improved or reformed
senses.example: He is an incorrigible flirt.

senses.definition: incapable of making mistakes or being wrong
senses.example: Even the best doctors are not infallible.

senses.definition: insulting, abusive or highly critical language
senses.example: The debate descended into a stream of invective.

senses.definition: fond of or characterized by joking; humorous or playful
senses.example: He made a jocular remark to ease the tension.

senses.definition: displaying or having a disinclination for physical exertion or effort; slow and relaxed
senses.example: They spent a languid afternoon by the pool.

senses.definition: full of or shedding light; bright or shining, especially in the dark
senses.example: The watch has luminous hands.

senses.definition: very intelligent or enlightening
senses.example: Her luminous essays changed how critics saw the poet.

senses.definition: to speak about someone in a spitefully critical manner
senses.example: He felt he had been unfairly maligned by the press.

senses.definition: evil in nature or effect; harmful
senses.example: The film explores the malign influence of a cult leader.

senses.definition: extremely unpleasant; repulsive
senses.example: He found the task of firing staff odious.

senses.definition: an outcast
senses.example: After the scandal, he became a pariah in political circles.

senses.definition: expressing contempt or disapproval
senses.example: "Bureaucrat" is often used in a pejorative sense.

senses.definition: a large or excessive amount of something
senses.example: The report contains a plethora of statistics.

senses.definition: recklessly extravagant or wasteful in the use of resources
senses.example: The government was accused of profligate spending.

senses.definition: licentious; dissolute
senses.example: He regretted the profligate years of his youth.

senses.definition: to forbid, especially by law
senses.example: The rules proscribe the use of phones during exams.

words.note: Proscribe means to forbid; prescribe means to recommend or order.

senses.definition: a short period of rest or relief from something difficult or unpleasant
senses.example: The rain brought a brief respite from the heat.

senses.definition: most noticeable or important
senses.example: The salient points of the report fit on one slide.

senses.definition: occurring at irregular intervals or only in a few places; scattered or isolated
senses.example: Sporadic gunfire could be heard through the night.

senses.definition: to demand or specify a requirement, typically as part of an agreement
senses.example: The contract stipulates that payment be made within thirty days.

senses.definition: (especially of something written or spoken) briefly and clearly expressed
senses.example: Her answer was succinct and to the point.

senses.definition: bad-tempered and sulky; gloomy
senses.example: The sullen teenager refused to come to dinner.

senses.definition: behaving or looking as though one thinks one is superior to others
senses.example: The supercilious clerk looked us up and down.

senses.definition: showing or motivated by susceptibility to bribery
senses.example: The venal official sold permits to the highest bidder.

words.note: Venal means corrupt; venial means minor and forgivable.

senses.definition: having a thick, sticky consistency between solid and liquid
senses.example: Honey is a viscous liquid.
